title: Five deep GCMT pairs had the larger event first in 1982-1999, but three groups gave an inconclusive exact test
abstract: We tested whether larger-first order in deep earthquake pairs extends to the earlier Global CMT record. Both reference depths were above 300 km and both moment magnitudes were at least 5.8. Pairs were within 200 km and seven days, with a magnitude gap of at least 0.5. In 1982-1999, all five eligible pairs had the larger event first. They occupied only three connected groups. An exact two-sided test of independent fair group signs gave p = 0.25. Thus, this earlier sample agrees in direction but gives inconclusive support under the test. A constant 100% group bootstrap range did not measure population uncertainty. Exact binomial limits for positive group signs were 29.2-100%. Secondary 1982-2020 results had 16 of 16 larger-first pairs in eight groups, with p = 0.0078125, but overlap prior evidence. Sparse groups, fixed selection, catalog error and group independence limit inference. The result does not identify direct triggering. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a separate audit, a repeat check and a figure are included. External source records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Deep pair shares and conditional group-sign limits. A constant bootstrap range does not measure population uncertainty.

citations.reason: Prior deep ComCat order result defines the earlier-period question. No event overlap with the primary test.
